La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

Shows a Waterkotte heat pump in Gladys through the local web interface of its
controller (EcoTouch, or the older EasyCon), without any cloud. Unofficial:
not affiliated with Waterkotte. **Never tested with a real heat pump**: it was
written from the open source Home Assistant integration
[ha-waterkotte](https://github.com/marq24/ha-waterkotte) and tested against a
simulated controller. Please report what you see on yours.

## What you get

One device, "Waterkotte heat pump", with what its controller gives:

- temperatures: outside, flow, return and return target, heating demand,
  source inlet and outlet, buffer tank, room (when a sensor is connected),
  hot water and hot water demand;
- compressor running, heating hot water, alarm;
- electric power (kW), heat output (kW), COP;
- **Heating** and **Hot water**: Off, Auto or Manual;
- **Hot water setpoint** (°C).

The values are read every 60 seconds (30 to 600, in the configuration).

## Setting up

1. Find the IP address of the heat pump (its web page) and give it a fixed
   address in your router.
2. In Gladys, open the integration's configuration: enter the address, choose
   the controller (**EcoTouch** when the web page asks for a password, even
   when it shows "EasyCon"; **EasyCon** for the older controllers without a
   login page), the user name (`waterkotte` unless your installer changed it)
   and the password of the web page. Save.
3. Add the heat pump from the **Discovery** tab.

The password is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only
to the heat pump. The web page is plain HTTP: keep the heat pump on a trusted
network.

### Sessions

The controller accepts few sessions at once (two according to ha-waterkotte;
its web page open in a browser uses one) and closes an idle one after about 5
minutes: after a restart of Gladys, the previous session may stay taken that
long. Gladys keeps a single session open, ends it when it stops or when the
configuration changes (saved several times in a row: applied one after the
other, the last one saved wins), and logs in again at most once
per read or per command, never in a loop. When the controller answers "too
many users", Gladys pauses for 1 minute, then 2, 4... up to 6 hours, and says
so in the configuration screen. When it refuses the user name or the
password, Gladys stops trying: correct them and save, or click **Test the
connection** (one try per click).

## Commands

**Off** (heating or hot water) is a stop: it does not depend on the "Allow
the commands" option, a pause or a read in progress. It is written, then read
back:

- read back Off: done;
- otherwise Gladys answers "not sent", "sent, without confirmation" or "not
  applied yet", keeps the stop (also across a restart) and writes it with the
  next reads: written again 3 times at most, and dropped 15 minutes after the
  click whatever the reads. Once written, it is not written again over a
  value someone else set after the click (on the controller, its web page);
  an older command of Gladys does not count. A stop not written yet is tried
  again 10 seconds later, then every minute; during a pause too, until its
  15 minutes (one login a minute at most). Such a stop can thus leave up to
  15 minutes after the click, once, over a setting made on the controller
  in between.

Off is refused, nothing sent, in these cases only:

- the controller is EasyCon (read only in this integration);
- the address or the password is missing: the stop is kept and written as
  soon as the configuration is complete (15 minutes at most);
- the heat pump refused the credentials before: the stop is kept and written
  once they are corrected (15 minutes at most);
- nothing could be written within 3 seconds (no answer, network down, a
  login refused "too many users"): the stop is kept and written by the next
  reads.

**Auto**, **Manual** and the **hot water setpoint** are refused unless you
turn on **Allow the commands** (off by default). Then:

- the hot water setpoint takes whole degrees from 28 °C to the ceiling of
  the configuration, **65 °C by default**, 40 to 65 °C (never more than
  65 °C, whatever is typed): scalding risk;
- each command reads the value and the serial number of the heat pump just
  before writing, and succeeds only when a read back shows the value asked;
- a command refused or cancelled says "nothing sent"; one sent without an
  answer says "sent, without confirmation" and the value is read again 5 and
  20 seconds later;
- a command clicked before an Off of the same value (or a hot water setpoint
  clicked before a hot water Off) never leaves after it.

The integration has no switch: a "turn everything off" of a voice assistant
or a scene never reaches the heat pump.

## Limits

- One heat pump per integration. Its serial number is checked at every read
  and before every command: when another heat pump answers at the address,
  nothing is published and the commands other than Off are refused.
- The controller answers one request at a time: when it is slow (more than
  about half a second per request), a scene changing several values at once
  may see the last ones refused "did not answer in time, nothing sent".
- EasyCon: read only, and its tags are those of EcoTouch (unchecked).
- The tag list comes from ha-waterkotte; Waterkotte publishes none.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Waterkotte te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your heat pump | `section` | No | Shows your Waterkotte heat pump (EcoTouch controller, or the older EasyCon) in Gladys through its local web interface, without any cloud: temperatures, compressor, hot water, alarm, and optionally the operation of heating and hot water and the hot water setpoint. Enter the IP address of the heat pump (give it a fixed address in your router) and the password of its web page, save, then add it from the Discovery tab. The controller accepts few sessions at once: Gladys keeps one open. The web page is plain HTTP: keep the heat pump on a trusted network. Never tested with a real heat pump. Not affiliated with Waterkotte. |
| IP address of the heat pump | `string` | Sí | The address of its web page: an IPv4 address or a host name (port 80 unless you add one, for example 192.168.1.50:8080). |
| Controller | `select` | No | EcoTouch when the web page asks for a password (even when it shows "EasyCon"); EasyCon for the older controllers without a login page (read only here). |
| User name | `string` | No | The user of the web page: waterkotte unless your installer changed it. |
| Password | `secret` | No | The password of the web page of the heat pump. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the heat pump. |
| Allow the commands | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: Gladys may set heating and hot water to Auto or Manual and change the hot water setpoint, up to the ceiling below. Off: those are refused. Turning heating or hot water Off does not depend on this option. |
| Hot water ceiling (°C) | `number` | No | Scalding risk: Gladys never sets the hot water above this temperature. 65 °C by default, from 40 to 65 °C (never more than 65 °C, whatever is typed). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the heat pump is read, in seconds. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the device and features added from now on, for the options and for the command errors. |

## Cómo instalar Waterkotte en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Waterkotte aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-waterkotte:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-waterkotte](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-waterkotte).

Waterkotte requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Waterkotte es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
